items.q: Eskandar has called them rich kids; Hooman answers that they all own factories. Does this punch line land?
before: Hooman said:
– Yeah, all of us own factories.
Eskandar lifted his head from the carpet and looked at Hooman with wide eyes. Hooman continued:

items.text: – Shit-for-brains. You make me open my mouth and say it. I mean, did you only hear about it? Weren't you hit by it yourself?
items.q: Hooman snaps at Eskandar, a roommate he finds annoying. Does this sound like a young man's natural crude talk?
before: – Heard?
– Yeah, well, word got around the university.

items.q: Hooman curses their bad luck with university places. Does it sound natural from an angry young man?
before: Hooman sighed and turned away from Farid. His gaze fell on Eskandar, and he shouted in a voice full of pain, like a needle sinking into an old wound:

items.text: – Man, don't talk to this one so politely; it'll go to his head. We took all those practice tests and ended up roommates with this antique.
items.q: Hooman sneers at his odd roommate Eskandar, calling him an antique. Does this sound natural?
before: Hooman said:

items.text: – You're the biggest cow of all. You've got the build for it too.
items.q: In Persian, calling someone a cow means a dull fool. Eskandar says this to heavy-set Hooman. Does the jab land?
before: – Eat the head of my dick, man. We've had enough of you. What do you know about what electrical engineering at Sharif means? And besides, did anyone ask your opinion?

items.text: – Murderous moves like this are just what I'd expect from you, but what I really want to know is what fucking maniac had his shop open at six on a Friday morning so you could go and buy a camera from him.
items.q: Hooman ribs Farid for buying a camera at dawn on a Friday. Does this sound like natural dorm banter?
before: – Look what camera I bought.
Hooman said, while examining the camera box:

items.text: – If Kamyar hadn't been such a precious little shit and had stayed in the dorm, no bed would have opened up and landed us with these two marvels.
items.q: Hooman grumbles about the two odd roommates they got stuck with. Does this sound natural and crude enough?

Eskandar stared for a moment at the corners of the few books jutting out from under my bed, then crawled on all fours toward Bahman's books. He lowered his head and looked at Bahman's books. Hooman said:

items.text: What did being top of the class and, I don't know, getting a second degree add to the length of my dick, when now my job is inspecting electrical substations?
items.q: Years later, Hooman scoffs at his student ambitions. Does 'add to the length of my dick' sound natural?
before: – What do you mean, those were the days, Doctor? I shit on those days and on the way we thought. Truly, I shit on all that perfectionism and double-majoring and being one of the best and a thousand other plagues and poisons.

items.text: – Leopard Farid, control your nerves and don't make a murderous move.
items.q: Hooman jokingly warns hot-headed Farid not to do anything rash. Is 'murderous move' clear for that?

items.text: – Leopard Farid can't even make up his own mind. One minute he's pulling murderous moves; the next he's saying, "Oh, blood. That made my skin crawl."
items.q: Hooman teases Farid, who loves reckless stunts but is squeamish about blood. Does the teasing land?

items.text: – Eagle Eye, may God not forgive you, you destroyed my back. Why don't you wear your glasses?
items.q: Half-blind Sajad has trodden on Eskandar. Does 'may God not forgive you' sound natural as an angry outburst?
before: Eskandar said in a voice that showed he could barely breathe:

items.text: – Eagle Eye, God has already struck Fly; don't you strike him too. For your mother's sake, don't walk around the room without your glasses.
items.q: Eskandar pleads with clumsy, short-sighted Sajad. Does 'For your mother's sake' sound natural here?

items.text: The important thing is that whenever I go to the supermarket, I pay money, buy my milk and cake, and put them in my body.
items.q: Hooman, who loves food, shrugs off talk of Bitcoin. Does 'put them in my body' sound funny and natural?
